summary: Most visitors need a Burundian visa, which the migration authority (CGM) issues online, at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport or at embassies; the single-entry visa allows a stay of one month. East African Community citizens receive a free EAC visa of up to six months at the CGM or any point of entry.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office describes Burundi as a largely cash-based society: take US dollars dated after 2006, as most businesses will not accept or exchange older notes and notes with small tears are rejected; euros and British pounds can usually be exchanged. Outside Bujumbura credit and debit cards are rarely accepted and there are not many ATMs, so do not rely on cash withdrawals; mobile money can often be used in tourist hotels. There is a shortage of foreign currency and an unofficial exchange rate that can differ substantially from the official one.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to the Mugina, Cibitoke, Bukinyayana, Bubanza and Mpanda communes and to the RN6 and RN10 roads through the Kibira National Park, because of a rebel group and possible armed incursions from the DR Congo, and advises against travelling by road outside Bujumbura after dark. Canada advises avoiding non-essential travel to Burundi.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to several communes and roads near the Kibira National Park and the border with the DR Congo, where armed-group activity has increased.

The UK Foreign Office advises taking US dollars dated after 2006, saying most businesses will not accept or exchange older notes and notes with small tears are rejected. It says outside Bujumbura cards are rarely accepted and ATMs are few, and advises not relying on cash withdrawals.

The Government of Canada says photographing sensitive installations — ports, military sites, government buildings and people in uniform — is prohibited. Always ask permission before photographing official buildings or individuals.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Burundi?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. Burundi's migration authority issues the single-entry visa (one month) online at migration.gov.bi, at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport or at embassies. Citizens of East African Community countries such as Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and Rwanda get a free EAC visa at the CGM or any point of entry instead.

faq.question: Which passports get a free visa at the border?
faq.answer: Citizens of the East African Community partner states — Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, South Sudan, the DR Congo and Somalia — need no visa in advance: the migration authority grants them a free 'EAC visa' at any point of entry, for stays of up to six months. It does not allow work.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Burundi?
faq.answer: Yes, at the airport: Burundi's migration authority says the entry visa is obtained online, at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport or at embassies, and it runs an online application for the airport entry visa. The transit visa (USD 40, three days) is issued at any point of entry.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Burundi?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK and Canadian travel advice both say a yellow fever vaccination certificate is required to enter Burundi, whichever country you arrive from.

faq.question: Is Burundi safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to parts of the north-west near the Kibira National Park and the DR Congo border, where armed-group activity and conflict have increased, and the Government of Canada advises avoiding non-essential travel to Burundi.
